text:
Answer engines change the way they cite sources, and the tools that read those citations get corrected, so in TextOS a series of observations can only be compared when the measurement method stays the same or carries an explicit version. Otherwise, a shift in the numbers may only mean that the ruler moved. In TextOS, the set of questions is treated as a measuring instrument: it defines what is observed, it can be explained and audited, it carries a version, and it cannot be changed once validated.

An automated test checks that the TextOS re-observation plan keeps both the version of the question set and the version of the measurement method. The preview record and the re-observation plan in TextOS point to the same draft and the same content fingerprints. That way, the article being followed is the one that was previewed, not a later variant of it.
